lesson_title: Count the Legs, Name the Beast
hook_text: Is a spider an insect? Count its legs and the answer takes two seconds.
clip_script: Most animals on Earth have no backbone. The biggest group wears its skeleton on the outside, like a suit of armour, with jointed legs. These are the arthropods. Now count. Six legs and three body parts: insect. Bee, beetle, mosquito. Eight legs and two body parts, no feelers: arachnid. Spider, scorpion, tick. So no, a spider is not an insect. Ten or more legs, two pairs of feelers, breathes with gills: crustacean. Crab, prawn, lobster. But in the same rock pool live animals with no legs at all. Soft and squishy, gliding on one big foot. Molluscs. Snails carry one shell, mussels two. And the octopus? No shell at all, eight arms, and smart enough to open a jar.
visual_style: Whiteboard bug sketches with legs lighting up as they are counted, sorting into three columns; then a rock pool with a snail, a mussel and an octopus slipping out of a jar.
mood: Quick-fire counting game ending in wonder.
pacing: Snappy counts, a beat on the spider verdict, a playful octopus finish.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and sort every creepy-crawly you find.
